title: Open-world long playtest — a real adventurer's life
brief: Start a genuinely new Avereth campaign at Level 1. Choose your own available base class and two starter skills. Play an independent adventurer in an open sandbox, not a QA script: pursue interesting Guild contracts or private quests, exploration, paid work, relationships, training and sensible character progression. These are possibilities, not required achievements or a fixed route. Prepare before dangerous work: look for local shops and compare affordable weapons, armour and useful supplies early, rather than waiting until a defeat. Make turning combat loot and earnings into usable equipment a recurring personal goal. On an appropriate town visit after successful hunts, actively seek a suitable buyer and sell surplus monster materials and other expendable loot at real offered prices. Keep equipped gear, quest cargo/proof and supplies you still need; do not sell them indiscriminately. Use the proceeds and quest earnings to visit a relevant equipment merchant, request concrete affordable weapon or armour offers, compare them with your current gear, and buy a useful upgrade when one is genuinely available and affordable. Actually equip it and check the engine outcome before relying on it in later adventures; carrying an item is not the same as equipping it. Check what you already own, current HP/MP, recovery options and the cost of food, sleep or lodging. Save for an upgrade or earn money through safer work if necessary; do not repeat shop visits without new money or useful stock. Buy only real available goods at real prices, and verify the engine booked the purchase and equipment. If prices are unknown, ask for an offer instead of merely saying you might shop later. If no suitable buyer, stock or affordable upgrade is available, pursue another sensible opportunity and revisit after circumstances change; do not loop over the same refusal, invent a transaction or buy useless gear just to satisfy the test. Shopping need not interrupt urgent situations or happen every turn. Assess the number and apparent strength of enemies before engaging; a quest label alone does not make a group safe. Choose easier work, recover, withdraw early or abandon a poor plan when sensible. No compulsory or suicidal fights, forced farming, free money, injected XP, fixtures, synthetic gear or invented accomplishments. Retry blocked plans when new evidence or a different approach helps; otherwise find another opportunity instead of repeating fruitless conversations or unrewarded chores. Roleplay and voluntary detours remain welcome. Keep playing naturally through the 100-turn observation window; stop only for death, a genuinely blocking failure or its normal end.

milestones.goal: Create a genuine Level-1 character with your own base class and starter-skill choices.
Keep playing freely until the 100th actual player turn, following your own goals. This is an observation window, not an achievement checklist; do not waste turns to reach the count.

focus: Observe whether quests can be accepted, progressed, completed and rewarded consistently, if you naturally pursue them.
Notice whether guild membership, rest, sleeping in town, travel, earning/spending money and equipment upgrades are useful and intuitive if they arise.

Act on the loot-to-gear goal during suitable town visits: sell surplus combat loot to a willing buyer, use real proceeds/rewards for a useful affordable upgrade, equip it, and observe it in later freely chosen adventures. Check actual inventory, coin and equipment changes; a narrated sale or purchase alone is not success.
Watch whether combat, resource use, leveling, training and organic skills/passives feel rewarding rather than repetitive.
Note meaningful inconsistencies between narrator, inventory, HUD, contracts, money, time, NPC actions and engine decisions.
Avoid forcing encounters or repeatedly chasing a fleeing animal just to advance a test. Make believable choices and move on when appropriate.
Keep your messages short and natural. System panels are helpful when needed, not a task to request every turn.
personas: independent cautious adventurer: explore, talk to people, assess risks, spend rewards on practical needs
curious opportunist: pursue interesting work and discoveries, develop your own ambitions
pragmatic mercenary: value profitable reasonable contracts and gear improvements without reckless fights
